wine.name: Kopar Cuvée
wine.grapes: Cabernet Franc and Merlot lead, with Cabernet Sauvignon a tenth at most; the first vintage, 1997, was Cabernet Sauvignon and Merlot in equal parts with some Cabernet Franc.
wine.sites: Named for the Kopár vineyard on the southern slope of Szársomlyó between Villány and Nagyharsány, where the soil is so thin that the limestone shows; the house's notes for the 2022 also name Csillagvölgy, Konkoly and Ördögárok.
wine.making: Made only in the vintages the house judges strong enough. By the house's notes the 2022 aged for sixteen months in small oak barrels, four fifths of them new and the rest in their second use; the first vintage, 1997, spent eighteen months in new barriques. The vineyards have been farmed organically since 2010.
wine.glass: Ripe plum and blackcurrant with black pepper, cigar box and toasted barrel spice, then cinnamon, graphite and tobacco as it opens; full and warm, with fine grained tannin. Older bottles turn to dried fruit and a savoury, tea like note.
wine.ageing: Young Kopar is firm; the house expects a strong vintage to keep for twenty years and more, and old bottles show dried fruit and a savoury edge.
wine.serve: 16 to 18 degrees Celsius; decant a young bottle for an hour or two; a Bordeaux glass.

label.means: The name of the Kopár vineyard; the word means barren, for its thin soil over limestone.
The protected wine district in the far south of Hungary, red country on a limestone ridge.

records.table: The bare limestone of a Szársomlyó slope gives Gere's Kopar Cuvée its name: Cabernet Franc and Merlot with a little Cabernet Sauvignon, aged in mostly new small oak. Ripe and peppery, with plum and cigar box, it rewards an hour in a decanter.
records.story: The Gere family speaks of seven generations of winemaking in Villány, but its modern story begins with the end of communism. In 1992 the family bottled its first Phoenix Cuvée, a blend it has made every year since and named, as the house tells it, for the town's revival after the political change. In the same year it founded a joint winery in Villány with the Weninger family of Burgenland, bringing Austrian cellar technique south. Then came the wine that made the house's name. After a group of Villány growers travelled to Bordeaux, the family blended Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot and Cabernet Franc from its own sites with the 1997 vintage, aged it in new barriques and named it Kopar, after its vineyard: a fanciful name was itself new in Hungary in the 1990s. The house counts the 2000 as Kopar's first classic vintage. From 2006 the blend turned towards Cabernet Franc and Merlot, and from 2010 the vineyards were farmed organically. In 2024 Kopar joined the reference collection in the cellar of the Cité du Vin in Bordeaux. Kopar is Villány's Bordeaux blend in the Gere form: Cabernet Franc and Merlot from limestone, made only in the years the house judges strong enough.

wine.name: Bock Capella
wine.grapes: Cabernet Franc, the larger part, with Cabernet Sauvignon at about a third and a little Merlot.
wine.sites: Cabernet Franc from the Ördögárok vineyard in the 2012, though the house's Hungarian sheet for the 2006 names Fekete-hegy, with Cabernet Sauvignon from Jammertal, the family's historic vineyard.
wine.making: Made only in the years the house judges exceptional, from lots selected in its vineyards. The wine is aged for about two years in new oak barrels before bottling, and the house holds older vintages back, selling some as museum lots long after the harvest.
wine.glass: Dried plum, dark chocolate and tobacco over black cherry and sweet barrel spice; full and warm in alcohol, with dense, polished tannin.
wine.ageing: Built for the cellar after two years in new oak, it opens after about ten years and holds for a decade beyond in a strong vintage.
wine.serve: 16 to 18 degrees Celsius; decant a young bottle for an hour; a Bordeaux glass.

label.means: Latin for a chapel; the house has a domed round cellar in Villány it calls the Bock chapel.

records.table: Bock makes Capella, Latin for a chapel, only in the years it judges exceptional: Cabernet Franc from Ördögárok, Cabernet Sauvignon from Jammertal and a little Merlot, two years in new oak. Ripe and dense, it carries dried plum and dark chocolate.
records.story: The Bock family counts nine generations of growers in Villány, and the Jammertal vineyard has long been its own. In 1981, after his father's death, the founder of the modern estate made his first harvest on his own account, and by Magyar Bor's account the house first bottled its wine in 1987. When private estates returned after 1990 the family built quickly: in 1991 it made its first Bock Cuvée, the blend that has since carried the house's name, and the estate grew into one of the large private cellars of the district, with cellars running under the town, a hotel, the Ermitage, and a restaurant beside it. Capella came as the house's own selection, a blend made only in the years it judges exceptional, Cabernet Franc led and aged two years in new oak; vintages such as 2006, 2007, 2008, 2009 and 2012 were made. Its name is the Latin for a chapel, and the house has a domed round cellar it calls the Bock chapel, where it holds tastings; the 2008 Capella was poured when its dome was consecrated. In 2021 the house marked forty years since that first harvest. Capella is the Villány idea at full weight: Cabernet Franc, warm southern slopes and long new oak.

wine.name: Duennium
wine.grapes: A blend whose mix moves with the year: the 2012 was Cabernet Franc, Cabernet Sauvignon and Syrah; by the estate's sheets Merlot led the 2006 and Cabernet Sauvignon the 2017.
wine.sites: Selected parcels of the estate's own vineyards on Fekete-hegy, the Black Hill above Kisharsány between Villány and Siklós, planted from 1992 onwards.
wine.making: Each lot ages apart in 225 litre barrels, mostly of Hungarian oak: seventeen months in vintages such as 2011, 2012 and 2015, half in new barrels and half in barrels a year old, and longer in 2006 and 2017. The cellar then picks the lots with most character and blends them; in 2012 and 2015 the blend rested a further year in large wooden casks before bottling.
wine.glass: Dark forest fruits, dried plum and blueberry with cedar, cinnamon, clove and star anise, and dark chocolate in warm years; full, with velvety, ripe tannin and lively acidity.
wine.ageing: Made to keep, it grows deeper and more savoury over ten years and more, and the house has offered its 2006 in magnum long after release.
wine.serve: 16 to 18 degrees Celsius; decant a young bottle for an hour; a Bordeaux glass.

records.table: On the Black Hill above Kisharsány, Vylyan ages each lot of Duennium apart in Hungarian oak and blends only the strongest, in vintages the estate judges fit. The result is full and velvety, with dried plum, cedar and clove.
records.story: By the estate's account Villány was Viliannak to the Romans and Vylyan in fifteenth century documents, and the founder chose that old name for his estate. He bought the base of the estate at Kisharsány in 1988, and in 1992 the cellar was founded and planting began on Fekete-hegy, the Black Hill between Villány and Siklós, with the winery built in the middle of the vines. The first bottled wines, a Kékoportó and a Cabernet Sauvignon, followed in 1994, and by the estate's account the Kékoportó won a gold medal at once. The founder died suddenly in 2004, and his widow took on the running of the estate. In 2008 Vylyan was named Winery of the Year in Hungary. Duennium is its answer to the Bordeaux blend: made only in the vintages the house judges fit, each lot aged apart in oak and only the lots with most character blended. The 2012, for instance, was Cabernet Franc, Cabernet Sauvignon and Syrah, seventeen months in barrique and a further year in a large cask. Duennium speaks for the district's younger estates: chosen lot by lot rather than to a fixed recipe, so its grapes change from year to year.

wine.name: Cuvée 7 Villány
wine.grapes: Cabernet Sauvignon leads, with Cabernet Franc and Merlot.
wine.sites: Three vineyards: Ördögárok, which gives the Cabernet Sauvignon at its base, and Kopár with its neighbour Konkoly on the southern face of Szársomlyó, where the wooded north side of the hill sends down cooling air.
wine.making: Aged for about fifteen months in French oak barrels of 225 and 500 litres, about a third of them new. The wine is then given about two years in bottle at the estate before it is released.
wine.glass: Cassis and blackcurrant with cedar, graphite and a little tobacco over sweet barrel spice; polished and full, with ripe, fine tannin and a long, warm finish.
wine.ageing: Released after its two years in bottle, it drinks well from then and gains cedar and savoury depth over the next five to ten years.
wine.serve: 16 to 18 degrees Celsius; decant a young bottle for an hour; a Bordeaux glass.

records.table: Three Villány sites, Ördögárok, Kopár and Konkoly, go into Sauska's Cuvée 7 Villány, a Cabernet Sauvignon led blend given fifteen months in French oak and two years in bottle before release. Polished and full, with cassis and cedar, it opens with an hour of air.
records.story: Sauska is a young house. By its own account a couple who had built a business abroad shared a dream of a family winery in Hungary, and it came true in Tokaj in 2003; the Villány estate followed, its first harvest in 2006. From the start the house built its Villány range on the Bordeaux grapes and on a few named sites under Szársomlyó: Kopár, which the estate calls the warmest vineyard in Hungary for its southern face, Konkoly beside it, cooled by the wooded north side of the hill, and Ördögárok. Cuvée 7 drew the three together and became the estate's flagship. Its 2007 vintage, from an estate barely two harvests old, won a regional trophy at the Decanter World Wine Awards. Later the estate made a second Cuvée 7 from its sites at Siklós, in the west of the district, led by Merlot from the Makár vineyard on loess, so the label names which of the two is in the bottle. Its Villány bottling carries the district's southern slopes through Cabernet Sauvignon, polished by French oak and a long rest in bottle.

wine.name: Kúria Cabernet Franc
wine.sites: The Köves-föld vineyard at Máriagyűd, by Siklós in the west of the district; the name means stony ground.
wine.making: From grapes farmed organically since 2009, with organic certification for the Kúria wines. The wine is matured in oak barrels and bottled without filtering, as every wine of the Kúria range is; by the estate's account its founder brought fermentation on fine lees and unfiltered bottling to the district.
wine.glass: Violet and blackberry with dark cherry, a leafy, grassy note of Cabernet Franc and sweet barrel spice; concentrated yet fresh, with fine, firm tannin and a long finish.
wine.ageing: Concentrated and oaky in youth, it is made to keep: the estate has offered vintages as old as 2002 and 2004 long after release.
wine.serve: 16 to 18 degrees Celsius; decant a young bottle for an hour, an old one gently off its sediment; a Bordeaux glass.

records.table: Grown organically on the stony Köves-föld vineyard at Máriagyűd, Malatinszky's Kúria Cabernet Franc is a single variety red, aged in oak and bottled unfiltered. Concentrated and fresh, with violet and blackberry, it should be decanted off any sediment.
records.story: By the estate's account the family's roots in wine lie by Lake Balaton, among landowning ancestors generations back. The modern estate is the work of a sommelier of the Budapest restaurant Gundel who, as the estate tells it, left in 1991 and soon opened a specialist wine shop in the capital. He began making his own wine in Villány in 1994, and in 1997 the winery was built and the estate set up again under the old name of a manor, a kúria. From the start the house set itself apart in the cellar: by its own account it brought fermentation on fine lees and unfiltered bottling to the district, and its Kúria range, above Noblesse, is bottled without filtering. In 2009 the estate turned to organic farming, and the Kúria wines carry organic certification. In the following years the district gave Cabernet Franc a designation of its own, Villányi Franc, and the grape became Villány's emblem. The Kúria Cabernet Franc, from the stony Köves-föld vineyard at Máriagyűd, had already shown the grape alone. Here Villány Cabernet Franc has no blend to hide behind: concentrated, organic and unfiltered.

It was fined with chalk from Siklós
It was aged under flor in cask
questions.exp: Every Kúria wine is bottled without filtering, so sediment can form; it is a red table wine, never a wine aged under flor.

questions.q: In which year was the Malatinszky Kúria estate set up and its winery built in Villány?
questions.exp: The winery was built and the estate set up in 1997; 1994 was the founder's first wine in Villány and 2009 the turn to organic farming.

sources.title: Magyar Bor: Malatinszky Kúria Organikus Szőlőbirtok
Hungarianwines: Malatinszky, a winemaker who cooks well

report: The house carries the living founder's name, so the prose says the founder; his Gundel years and the wine shop rest on the estate's own page and are hedged.
1997 and organic farming from 2009 rest on the estate and Magyar Bor; one directory page denies the organic status and is set aside.
Whether the Kúria Cabernet Franc carries the words Villányi Franc on its label was not confirmed, so the label lists the grape and the district only.
The length and kind of oak ageing were not found; the making says aged in oak, from barrel sample notes and a reviewer, and gives no figure.
The glass rests on published notes for the 2009 and 2015 in sources whose addresses carry a living name, so they are not listed.
The region record does not list this house; the plan's why is borne out, and the house could be added to the region's producers line.

changed: story: the family's roots were "in Badacsony ... in the eighteenth century"; one source has the family by Lake Balaton from the fourteenth century, so now by Lake Balaton, generations back, by the estate's account.
story: leaving Gundel in 1991 is the estate's account, and one source has the sommelier there from 1990 to 1994; now hedged as the estate tells it.
wine.label, story and traps: the Kúria range was "above Signature and Noblesse"; the estate's own page gives Le Sommelier, Noblesse and Kúria, so now above Noblesse.
wine.making: "certified since 2009" was more than the sources say; now farmed organically since 2009, with organic certification for the Kúria wines (bor.hu).
others: Noblesse Cabernet Sauvignon was not found; now Noblesse Cabernet Franc, listed in the estate's shop (shop.malatinszky.hu).
open: The 1991 wine shop rests on the estate's page alone.
